description: Instamojo’s store vs GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce: plans, its fee per payment against Razorpay, cash on delivery, shipping — and who each one suits.

h1: Instamojo store alternative: GoCommerce vs Instamojo
tagline: Instamojo sells payments and gives you a store. GoCommerce is the store, and you pick the payments.
lede: Instamojo is a payment gateway first, and its online store comes with that gateway built in: nothing to connect, and a fee of 5% plus a fixed amount on each payment — 2% plus the fixed amount on the Growth plan billed yearly. GoCommerce is a backend you run, paired with a gateway you choose, or a store hosted on kitcommerce.store for {hostedFee} of each successful sale. On Growth the fees are close; the difference is who owns the store.

5% plus a fixed fee on Lite and Starter, 2% plus a fixed fee on Growth billed yearly, each plus GST — and covering the gateway, which Instamojo says comes at no additional charge.
None from GoCommerce when you run it yourself: the gateway charges its own rate, and Razorpay lists 2% + GST. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets, pay later and EMI through Instamojo, with an option to pass the fee on to the buyer.
Whatever your gateway offers, through one of eleven payment modules — Razorpay, Cashfree, Stripe and Adyen among them.
Shipway, Shiprocket, Vamaship, Pickrr and others; Instamojo says pickup and delivery cover 26,000 pin codes.

Themes, with CSS customisation and JavaScript editing among the store features.
The source of the backend and storefront, checkout included.

No plan limits. Stock is tracked per location, as on hand and reserved.
Abandoned cart recovery, discount coupons and advanced analytics from Growth; Google Shopping and Facebook catalogue sync.
Discounts in the core; cart recovery, Google Merchant Center and Meta catalogue feeds, Klaviyo and newsletters as modules.

Webhooks, 342 documented REST operations, and an MCP server that lets AI agents work the store.
Yours when you run it — a single Go binary beside a PostgreSQL database, on any server you choose. Or hosted on kitcommerce.store, for {hostedFee} of each successful sale.

cost.note: From the published fees; GST is added on both sides. On Lite and Starter, Instamojo’s 5% is more than twice Razorpay’s standard 2%, before its fixed fee per payment. On Growth billed yearly the percentages match, and the gap is that fixed fee plus the plan — a sum that hosting and upkeep can easily outweigh. Against Instamojo, GoCommerce’s case is ownership, not fees.

themWhen: You want to take payments and sell today, with no gateway to apply for and nothing to host.
You are on Growth billed yearly: at 2% plus a fixed fee a payment, the store and the gateway cost about what a gateway alone would.
You sell a small catalogue and would rather pick a theme than touch code.
You also sell through payment links or landing pages, and want one Instamojo dashboard for all of it.
usWhen: You are on Lite or Starter and prepaid sales are growing — 5% plus a fixed fee a payment is more than twice Razorpay’s standard 2%.
You want to choose, or change, your payment gateway without changing your store.
You need catalogue depth the plans cap — more images per product, stock held at several locations.
You need several storefronts, B2B price lists or marketplace vendors.
takeOnExtra: The gateway account is yours to open: GoCommerce takes online payments only through a provider you sign up with.

faq.q: What does Instamojo charge per sale?
faq.a: Instamojo’s online store charges 5% plus a fixed fee per payment on Lite and Starter, and 2% plus a fixed fee on the Growth plan billed yearly, each plus GST. Its pricing page says the payment gateway comes integrated with no additional charges, so that fee covers payment processing.

faq.q: What store plans does Instamojo have?
faq.a: Lite is free. Starter is billed yearly, and Growth yearly or monthly; a store built for you by Instamojo’s team is priced on request. GST is charged on top of the plan prices.

Against Lite and Starter, once prepaid sales grow, if you run it yourself: Razorpay lists 2% + GST, against Instamojo’s 5% plus a fixed fee. Against Growth billed yearly, barely — the difference is the fixed fee per payment plus the plan, and a server can cost more than that. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale. Choose GoCommerce for ownership and depth, not to save on fees.

faq.q: Can I use Razorpay with GoCommerce?
faq.a: Yes, through the payments-razorpay module, which calls Razorpay’s API directly. Eight other payment modules — Stripe, Adyen and Hyperswitch among them — are there if you choose differently, and cash on delivery needs none.

faq.q: Can Svelte Commerce be the storefront for an Instamojo store?
faq.a: No. Instamojo is not among the 26 backends Svelte Commerce connects to. Paired with GoCommerce, Svelte Commerce reaches it through an early connector, 0.1.0, covering catalogue, cart, checkout and order lookup; customer accounts and search are not covered yet.
